20-minutes-till-dawn.title: 20 Minutes Till Dawn
20-minutes-till-dawn.notes: This game has a native macOS version on Steam, so the Mac Steam app runs it directly without Highball. The Windows build was reported perfect on DXMT after a 17-minute session on an M4. No measurement here yet.

2xko.title: 2XKO

9-kings.title: 9 Kings
9-kings.notes: This game has a native macOS version on Steam, so the Mac Steam app runs it directly without Highball. The Windows build was reported perfect through Highball after a 48-minute session, mode not stated. No measurement here yet.

a-game-about-digging-a-hole.title: A Game About Digging A Hole
a-game-about-digging-a-hole.notes: Playable on an M1 with DXMT on the default engine (r28) over 24 minutes, with the mouse cursor sometimes showing over the game.

a-memoir-blue.title: A Memoir Blue
a-memoir-blue.notes: Played start to finish on the default engine on an M1, beautifully at 1080p by the reporter's account, on DXMT and on Apple's DirectX 12 support. Quitting the game does not exit cleanly. On DXMT the game offered 4K while the Metal HUD showed 1080p, and on Apple's DirectX 12 support it offered 1080p at most. Nothing was measured here.

a-plague-tale-innocence.title: A Plague Tale: Innocence

a-short-hike.title: A Short Hike
a-short-hike.notes: Plays. Reported as running at full speed with no issues. The reporter did not say which chip, macOS version, engine or graphics mode, and no frame rate was measured, so this row records that it works and nothing more. Not tried here.

active-neurons-wonders-of-the-world.notes: Reported playable on D3DMetal (free to play). Between puzzle waves a subtitled narration plays over a black background, which looks like a video that does not show.

ad-infinitum.title: Ad Infinitum
ad-infinitum.notes: Playable on an M1 (Epic) at about 25 to 30 fps with every setting on Low and textures on Medium. It starts on the Epic preset, which is too heavy there.

aethermancer-demo.title: Aethermancer Demo
aethermancer-demo.notes: The demo of Aethermancer, a Unity 2022.3 game by moi rai games. Reported about 95 percent smooth at 100 fps over an hour and a half on DXMT with the Wine 11 engine, with short frame hiccups here and there, one of them a drop of about 2 seconds, which do not matter in the turn-based play. The run went through Proton-ish from the macOS Steam client, not through Highball itself. Nothing was measured here.

age-of-empires-ii-definitive-edition.title: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition
age-of-empires-ii-definitive-edition.notes: This game has a native macOS version on Steam, so the Mac Steam app runs it directly without Highball. age-of-history-3.title: Age of History 3
age-of-history-3.notes: Reported perfect after an 85-minute session on DXVK on an M5 Pro with macOS 26.6.2, long enough to cover real play rather than only the launch; frame rate not recorded yet.

age-of-mythology-retold.title: Age of Mythology: Retold
age-of-mythology-retold.notes: Reported perfect on D3DMetal on the Wine 11 engine r15 on an M4 Pro. Whether it starts without AVX advertised, in another graphics mode, or on the default engine was not reported, no frame rate was given, and nothing was…

agent-a-a-puzzle-in-disguise.notes: Doesn't get past the title screen in one report on an M1 with D3DMetal, the Epic copy. A Unity game, Direct3D 11.

aimlabs.title: Aimlabs

aion-2.title: AION 2
aion-2.notes: Does not start, NCGuard, the game's anti-cheat, stops it. With msync NCGuard exits about 8 seconds in with 0xE0000015 on a fresh environment (2 of 2 tries). With sync off NCGuard finishes its setup, then the game spins on its splash screen at about 157% CPU for over seven minutes without loading anything (3 of 3). With esync Steam crashes before the game starts (1 of 1).

akane.title: Akane
akane.notes: Reported perfect on an M4 Pro with DXMT on the default engine (r28) in a 5 minute session. The game also has a native Mac version on Steam.

amanda-the-adventurer.title: Amanda the Adventurer

aniimo.title: Aniimo
aniimo.notes: Reported playable with unspecified minor issues after a 54-minute session on DXMT on an M1 Pro with macOS 27; frame rate not recorded yet. Perfect again on an M5 Pro with DXMT from a short session (highball-db#670).

another-world-20th-anniversary-edition.title: Another World: 20th Anniversary Edition
another-world-20th-anniversary-edition.notes: Gets in game in one report on an M1 after about 45 seconds of black screen following Play and then Intro, on DXMT and WineD3D alike. It's a 32-bit game.

aperture-desk-job.notes: Re-verified on engine r2 on 2026-09-10: the Valve logo, the office scene and the Start/Options/Quit menu all render on DXVK at 30.8 fps, GPU bound at 29 ms per frame. The game puts up a 'Controller Required' banner and needs a gamepad to actually play, which is the game's own requirement. It also shows a 'This game has been optimized for play on the Steam Deck' notice on first run that has to be dismissed. DXVK is…

apex-legends.notes: EAC; Linux/Mac support explicitly dropped by Respawn in 2024

arc-raiders.title: ARC Raiders
arc-raiders.notes: An online game with Easy Anti-Cheat. Easy Anti-Cheat runs under Proton on Linux when a game allows it, but that support does not carry over to Wine on a Mac, so the game is not expected to get past its anti-cheat through Highball. The report did not say where it stopped.

armored-core-vi.title: Armored Core VI
armored-core-vi.notes: reported working via GPTK-class stacks. Reported playable on an M1 Pro with D3DMetal, offline with Easy Anti-Cheat skipped, borderless at 1440x810 on low settings. The first launch needs a lower macOS resolution to get through, see the known issues.

art-of-rally.title: art of rally
art-of-rally.notes: Plays. Reported as running fine. The only message seen was about the Steam overlay not being available because of a missing DLL, which does not affect the game. The reporter did not say which chip, macOS version, engine or graphics mode, and no frame rate was measured. Not tried here. A second reporter played the Epic copy for six minutes on DXMT on an M2 with macOS 27 and rated it perfect.

artillery-miner.title: Artillery Miner
artillery-miner.notes: Reported perfect on the default engine after five hours of play. The reporter did not say which graphics mode. No measurement here yet.

ascend-to-zero.title: Ascend to ZERO
ascend-to-zero.notes: Reported playable on DXMT, the default mode, with frame drops and a little stutter. The session was one minute, so this covers the start only.

assassins-creed-brotherhood.title: Assassin's Creed Brotherhood
assassins-creed-brotherhood.notes: Reported playable over two hours on an M1 with the default engine and DXMT, at 1680x1050 with the game's default settings, with freezes in some cutscenes. Nothing was measured here.

assassins-creed-syndicate.title: Assassin's Creed Syndicate
assassins-creed-syndicate.notes: Reported perfect on an M4 with DXMT over 7 minutes, on the Wine 11 engine (r27) with AVX advertised and a 60 fps cap. Whether AVX is needed is not known.

assassins-creed.title: Assassin's Creed
assassins-creed.notes: Plays in one report on an M1 on the Wine 11 engine r30 with athei's x87sidecar switched on (HB_X87SIDECAR=1 in the environment's variables, Highball 0.10.26) and DXVK, at about 40 fps (highball-db#901). Without the sidecar the title screen ran at about 7 fps, and D3DMetal crashed on the way in. Choose the controller in the game's settings at every start. It's a 32-bit game.

assetto-corsa-competizione.title: Assetto Corsa Competizione
assetto-corsa-competizione.notes: Unreal Engine 4, Direct3D 11. Reported perfect on DXMT after a short session of 8 minutes. No measurement here yet.

assetto-corsa.title: Assetto Corsa
assetto-corsa.notes: Works end to end with two things in place: install the .NET Framework 4.8 dependency first (bottle settings → Dependencies; took 6 minutes here on 2026-09-02, can take 20-40 and looks frozen — let it finish), and use the D3DMetal renderer. asteroids-recharged.title: Asteroids: Recharged
asteroids-recharged.notes: Reported perfect on a base M4 with D3DMetal on the default engine (r28) in a two minute session, so it covers the start only.

astral-ascent.title: Astral Ascent
astral-ascent.notes: Plays. Reported as a smooth 60 fps in gameplay, with drops to about 25 fps during the intro and cutscenes, and a DualShock 4 controller working. The reporter did not say which chip, macOS version, engine or graphics mode. Not tried here.

astrologaster.title: Astrologaster
astrologaster.notes: Steam has a Mac version too, which the reporter found broken (they are working with the developer). The Windows version through Highball starts but hangs on Loading after New Game or Continue, which matches a hang Windows players describe in the game's Steam discussions, so it may not be Highball's. The developer reproduced the hang and ties it to macOS 27 (highball-db#479, 2026-10-14). Since then the developer has…

astrometica.title: Astrometica
astrometica.notes: Reported playable with minor issues on DXMT after a session of only 3 minutes, so this says the game starts and renders, not that it holds up. No measurement here yet.

astroneer.title: ASTRONEER
astroneer.notes: Reported perfect on D3DMetal on the default engine on an M4. DXMT, the default mode, is untested, so the page does not pick a mode. No frame rate given. Also perfect on an A18 Pro (MacBook Neo) on the Wine 11 engine r30 with D3DMetal over 28 minutes (highball-db#1129).

atari-mania.title: Atari Mania
atari-mania.notes: Reported perfect on a base M4 with D3DMetal on the default engine (r28) in a three minute session, so it covers the start only.

atomic-heart.title: Atomic Heart
atomic-heart.notes: Reported playable on an M1 Pro with D3DMetal on Wine 11 engine r26 once its settings are tuned, at 110 fps or more on the main screen.

autonauts.title: Autonauts
autonauts.notes: Reported playable on an M1 with DXVK over 140 minutes after lowering bloom and other graphics settings.

aven-colony.title: Aven Colony
aven-colony.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT after a ten-minute session, so the report covers launch and the first minutes of a colony rather than a long game. No measurement here yet.

azeroth-survivors.title: Azeroth Survivors (艾澤拉斯倖存者)
azeroth-survivors.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT with the default engine. Where the game comes from is not known.

back-4-blood.title: Back 4 Blood
back-4-blood.notes: Doesn't start. The game needs Easy Anti-Cheat, which can't load under Wine on a Mac, so the launch stops at 'Failed to load the anti-cheat module' and no engine or graphics mode changes that.

backrooms-escape-together.title: Backrooms: Escape Together
backrooms-escape-together.notes: Reported playable on D3DMetal; the reporter says the other graphics modes half render the scene and the lights misbehave, so D3DMetal is the one to use. The microphone picked up their voice but friends could not hear them in game. No measurement here yet.

bad-cheese.title: Bad Cheese
bad-cheese.notes: Reported perfect on an M1 with D3DMetal over a short session.

bad-north-jotunn-edition.title: Bad North: Jotunn Edition
bad-north-jotunn-edition.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT after a session of 3 minutes. The reporter played the Epic copy; the Steam id here is the same game on Steam. No measurement here yet.

baldur-s-gate-3.title: Baldur's Gate 3
baldur-s-gate-3.notes: native mac build exists — prefer it; Wine works too. Reported playable through Highball in DirectX 11 mode with DXMT on the Wine 11 engine on an M5 (GOG edition), apart from the picture stretching when the aspect ratio was changed.

banished.title: Banished
banished.notes: Reported perfect on the default engine with Apple's DirectX 12 support on an M4 Pro after a short session. Nothing was measured here.

batman-arkham-knight.title: Batman: Arkham Knight
batman-arkham-knight.notes: Reported perfect on the Epic copy with the Wine 11 engine and DXMT on an M5 Pro over 14 minutes. Nothing was measured here.

batman-arkham-origins.title: Batman: Arkham Origins
batman-arkham-origins.notes: Reported perfect on an M4 Pro with DXMT over 22 minutes on the default engine (r26). On an M1 it plays on the Wine 11 engine r30 with DXMT, 102 fps average in the game's benchmark with athei's x87sidecar on (HB_X87SIDECAR=1), where engine r29 stuttered through its first screens and never reached the title screen (highball-db#978). A DualSense works through Steam Input. It's a 32-bit game.

batomon-showdown.title: Batomon Showdown
batomon-showdown.notes: Reported playable on DXMT on an M5, with occasional stuttering in the sound effects as the only complaint. No session length or frame rate was given and nothing was measured here. A second player rated it perfect over 88 minutes on an M1 with macOS 15.

battle-engine-aquila.title: Battle Engine Aquila
battle-engine-aquila.notes: Reported perfect on the default Wine 10 engine twice, once in DXVK mode over 5 minutes and once in Wine's own Direct3D mode over 21 minutes, both with Emulate display mode changes on, without which the game's resolution was wrong. The same player found it slow on the Wine 11 engine. Both modes worked, so the page sets no mode. No measurement here yet.

battle-realms-zen-edition.title: Battle Realms: Zen Edition
battle-realms-zen-edition.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT on the default engine after a one-minute session, so launch and the first screen rather than a full match. No measurement here yet.

battlebit-remastered.title: BattleBit Remastered
battlebit-remastered.notes: Cannot work. BattleBit Remastered uses Easy Anti-Cheat, which loads a kernel driver on Windows, and Wine cannot run one. The Proton runtime that makes EAC work on Linux has no macOS build. The reporter also notes that the game's offline mode cannot be reached without the anti-cheat installed, so there is no way around it from inside the game either.

bendy-and-the-ink-machine.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT on an M5 Max. The report was made on the Epic copy, so the Steam copy has not been reported. No session length or frame rate was given and nothing was measured here.

between-horizons.title: Between Horizons – A Sci-Fi Detective Adventure
between-horizons.notes: Reported perfect on an M1 with DXMT over 21 minutes.

beyond-two-souls.notes: Renders on DXMT. Start it from Highball's library: a game started from Steam's own window gets the environment's mode, not the one set on its page, and this game shows a black screen on DXVK.

bf6-redsec.title: Battlefield REDSEC
bf6-redsec.notes: Anti-cheat: EA anticheat. Linux/Proton status 'Denied' does not apply to macOS.

big-walk.title: Big Walk
big-walk.notes: A Unity game about talking to friends over voice. On the default engine with DXMT it opens on its microphone check, the first screen a player sees. Nothing past that was tried, and voice chat through Wine's audio input was not tested.

bionic-commando-rearmed.notes: Runs once NVIDIA's PhysX System Software is in the environment, which the recipe now installs (the reporter of highball#375 and #428 confirmed it on an M2 Max, 2026-10-26). Without it the game crashed on launch on DXVK and on Wine's own Direct3D alike: it starts a second copy of itself, loads PhysX's loader and cooking DLLs from its folder but never PhysXCore, and raises its own fatal error. Nothing was measured…

birds-organized-neatly.title: Birds Organized Neatly
birds-organized-neatly.notes: Reported perfect on the default engine on an M4.

black-mesa.title: Black Mesa
black-mesa.notes: Plays on the Wine 11 engine for the one player so far (M5 Pro, macOS 27.2) in Wine's own Direct3D, DXMT or Apple's DirectX 12 support, with some frame drops in heavy scenes, and the recipe makes Play offer that engine. bleach-brave-souls.title: BLEACH Brave Souls
bleach-brave-souls.notes: Reported playable on D3DMetal (free to play). After the logo the intro video stays black while its audio plays; it can be skipped after a few seconds, and the game does not play it again after the first start. It is a port of the mobile game, so some dialogs need the mouse even though a controller works in play.

blood-bowl-3.title: Blood Bowl 3
blood-bowl-3.notes: Reported playable on DXMT after a 40-minute session on an M3 with the steam and vcrun2022 recipes. The reporter gave 4 of 5 without saying what was less than perfect. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here.

bloodbreaker-labyrinth-of-the-witch-demo.title: Bloodbreaker: Labyrinth of the Witch Demo
bloodbreaker-labyrinth-of-the-witch-demo.notes: Reported playable on D3DMetal, where four GameMaker error boxes come up before the game starts and the game plays after OK on each. On an M4 the demo started on DXMT went straight to its Choose a Language screen with no box, while D3DMetal stopped at the first box, so DXMT is the mode to use. The game itself was not played here. The full game is a separate Steam app (3530380), not tested.

bloons-td-6.notes: This game has a native macOS version on Steam, so the Mac Steam app runs it directly without Highball. The Windows build was reported perfect on DXMT after an 11-minute session on an M5. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here.

blur.title: Blur
blur.notes: Bizarre Creations' 2010 racing game, assumed from the program's name, Blur. Not on Steam (no match in Steam's store search). Reported perfect on an M1 on the Wine 11 engine r31 in a one minute session, so it covers the start only.

bmx-streets.title: BMX Streets
bmx-streets.notes: Reported perfect on an M3 Max with DXMT on the default engine (r28) in a three minute session, so it covers the start only.

bodycam.title: Bodycam

On a base M5 the one report gets about 40 to 50 fps on the training ground and around 30 fps online with every setting low, TSR at Quality, and the render resolution at half the display's native. Playable, but the reporter's own verdict is that a shooter at 30 to 40…

bomber-crew.title: Bomber Crew
bomber-crew.notes: The menus and the mission preparation screen work, then the mission never starts and the menu freezes, on Wine's own Direct3D and on DXMT with Emulate display mode changes. The cause was not found: the launch log does not show the game's own errors and its Player.log was not sent. Bomber Crew also has a native Mac version on Steam, whose graphics quality is fixed at Low by the reporter's account.

bomjman.title: BOMJMAN
bomjman.notes: Reported perfect on an M1 with D3DMetal over 43 minutes.

boomerang-fu.title: Boomerang Fu
boomerang-fu.notes: Reported perfect on an M3 Max with D3DMetal over 3 minutes, on the Wine 11 engine (r29).

booster-pack-heroes-demo.title: Booster Pack Heroes Demo
booster-pack-heroes-demo.notes: A Unity 6 game. Reported playable on DXMT with Highball's Wine 11 engine, started through another tool, with a few short frame drops.

botany-manor.title: Botany Manor
botany-manor.notes: Reported playable on an M1 (Epic) with a limited resolution choice. The reporter prefers DXMT, which starts at 1024x768, over D3DMetal's squished 960x1080.

boxes-lost-fragments.title: Boxes: Lost Fragments
boxes-lost-fragments.notes: Reported perfect through the tutorial on an M1. No measurement here yet.

brawlhalla.title: Brawlhalla

ghostrunner-2.title: Ghostrunner 2

An Unreal Engine 4 game with a DirectX 12 path; D3DMetal was not tried. The Steam id here is the same game on Steam. No measurement here yet.

gi-joe-wrath-of-cobra.title: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra
gi-joe-wrath-of-cobra.notes: Reported playable on an M1 with D3DMetal (Epic).

grounded.notes: Reported playable on an M3 Pro with DXMT, multiplayer included, after two changes to the game's own DLLs.

gu-long-feng-yun-lu.title: 古龙风云录

Unity 2020.1, 64-bit, Direct3D 11. The store has no English title. No measurement here yet.

guild-wars-2.notes: Free to play on Steam, about 90 GB. gunsmith-simulator.title: Gunsmith Simulator

hack-n-slash.title: Hack 'n' Slash

half-life-2-deathmatch.title: Half-Life 2: Deathmatch

half-life.notes: The 1998 original (GoldSrc). Reported perfect after 8 minutes on an M3 Max on the default engine r17 with the environment on DXVK and the frame cap at 60. The game draws through OpenGL, which Wine hands to the Mac's own OpenGL whatever the graphics mode, so the mode is unlikely to matter for it, an inference rather than a measurement, and the mode here is the one reported. hell-clock.title: Hell Clock

injustice-gods-among-us-ultimate-edition.title: Injustice: Gods Among Us Ultimate Edition

last-evil.title: Last Evil
last-evil.notes: Playable on an M3 with DXMT on the default engine (r28) over 70 minutes, at a lower frame rate than the reporter sees on similar Windows hardware.

last-pirates-die-together.title: Last Pirates: Die Together
last-pirates-die-together.notes: Reported perfect after a six-minute session on DXMT on an M1; frame rate and longer play are not recorded yet.

left-4-dead-2.title: Left 4 Dead 2
left-4-dead-2.notes: Runs well on an M2 Air once workshop add-ons are not loaded automatically; with them the campaign froze at load on DXVK and crawled on Wine's Direct3D. left-4-dead.notes: Fullscreen fails: the game asks macOS for its display mode, Wine's Mac driver refuses, and the Source engine then cannot create its Direct3D device ("Failed to create D3D device!") whatever the graphics mode. Windowed and borderless works, and the row adds -windowed -noborder to the launch. Reported playable only on Wine's Direct3D, 15 to 20 fps on low settings on an M5; the other modes ran at 3 to 5 fps for the…

legends-of-idleon-mmo.title: Legends of Idleon MMO
legends-of-idleon-mmo.notes: Reported working but laggy over about 30 minutes, which the reporter puts down partly to the game being an MMO. Run through Proton-ish on Highball's Wine 11 engine, not through the Highball app. Nothing was measured here.

lego-batman-3-beyond-gotham.title: LEGO Batman 3: Beyond Gotham

lego-city-undercover.title: LEGO City Undercover
lego-city-undercover.notes: Reported perfect on the default engine with DXMT on an M4 MacBook Air: a steady 55 to 60 fps at the native 2560x1600 by the Metal HUD over 49 minutes, with small frame time spikes mostly at autosaves. Nothing was measured here.

lego-marvel-super-heroes.title: LEGO® MARVEL Super Heroes
lego-marvel-super-heroes.notes: The first level plays at 60 fps on DXVK on an M5 with an Xbox controller. The reporter needed -novid to get past the intro videos, and in-engine cutscenes miss some textures. Not measured here.

lego-star-wars-the-force-awakens.title: LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens
lego-star-wars-the-force-awakens.notes: Feral's Mac port runs on Apple silicon, and Steam for Mac installs it with the same Steam purchase, though the store page names Windows only and Steam's data never marks the build as 64-bit. Highball offers that Mac version. The Windows version has no report here yet.

lego-star-wars-the-skywalker-saga.title: LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga
lego-star-wars-the-skywalker-saga.notes: Reported playable on DXVK over a one-hour session on an M2, with minor issues the reporter did not describe. No measurement here yet.

lego-the-lord-of-the-rings.title: LEGO® The Lord of the Rings™
lego-the-lord-of-the-rings.notes: Plays on DXVK on an M5. The reporter had slowdowns at first and it ran smooth after lowering some settings in the game. Not measured here.

lego-voyagers.title: LEGO Voyagers
lego-voyagers.notes: Reported perfect on an M4 with DXMT over 92 minutes.

lethal-company.title: Lethal Company
lethal-company.notes: Boots with no configuration and runs smoothly at 120 fps on an M5 in the one Highball report, stable over a ten-minute session. Longer play and lobbies are not recorded yet. On an M2 with DXMT a player found a small input delay and occasional stutter, rating it 4 of 5 (highball-db#667).

life-is-strange-before-the-storm-remaste.title: Life is Strange: Before the Storm Remastered
life-is-strange-before-the-storm-remaste.notes: Reported playable for an hour on D3DMetal on an M5 Pro with the default engine. The one flaw reported is a picture that does not fill the screen. life-is-strange-remastered.notes: Reported perfect on D3DMetal with the GPTK 4 engine, which needs macOS 27, after a two-minute session. A second report played it perfectly for 54 minutes on the default Wine 10…

limbus-company.title: Limbus Company
limbus-company.notes: Reported perfect on D3DMetal on the default engine after a short session of 15 minutes. The game is free to play on Steam. No measurement here yet.

loftia-demo.title: Loftia Demo

luftrausers.title: LUFTRAUSERS
luftrausers.notes: Plays. Reported as playing fine. The reporter did not say which chip, macOS version, engine or graphics mode, and no frame rate was measured, so this row records that it works and nothing more. Not tried here.

lumina-veil.title: Lumina Veil

mage-arena.title: Mage Arena
mage-arena.notes: Reported playable with workarounds on the default engine with Apple's DirectX 12 support on an M1. meltdown-crew-demo.title: Meltdown Crew Demo
meltdown-crew-demo.notes: Reported perfect on an M4 with DXMT on the default engine (r28) over 70 minutes. The demo of Meltdown Crew (Steam app 4824220). Steam's store API gave no details for the demo's own id.

message-from-aliens-demo.title: Message From Aliens Demo
message-from-aliens-demo.notes: Reported perfect on an M5 Pro with DXMT on the default engine (r28) over six hours. The free demo of Message From Aliens (Steam app 1858720).

metro-last-light-redux.title: Metro: Last Light Redux
metro-last-light-redux.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT on the default engine (the Epic copy). Steam also sells a Mac version.

mi-chang-sheng.title: 觅长生

mindustry.title: Mindustry
mindustry.notes: Reported perfect on an M5 on the default engine (r28) in a 3 minute session. The game also has a native Mac version.

mini-settlers.title: Mini Settlers

vellum.title: Vellum
vellum.notes: Alvios Games' co-op roguelike, assumed from the program's name. Reported perfect on a base M2 with DXMT on the default engine (r28) over 13 minutes.

velocity-ultra.title: Velocity Ultra
velocity-ultra.notes: Launches, not playable. The game's pre-launcher (settings.exe, 32-bit) shows, and Play rarely brings the main window. The launch log has DXVK's 'Failed to create surface' twice and a stack overflow in settings.exe. A Direct3D 9 game, so in the D3DMetal and DXMT modes it goes through DXVK's Direct3D 9 on the default engine; With Wine's own Direct3D as the game's mode the pre-launcher crashes outright (0xc0000409, a…

viewfinder.title: Viewfinder
viewfinder.notes: Reported perfect on Wine's own Direct3D over 46 minutes. No measurement here yet. Perfect again on the Epic copy over 103 minutes, in a DXVK environment on an M2 with engine r28. A third player, on the Epic copy with DXMT on an M5, rated it 4 of 5 (highball-db#647): the first launch showed nothing until the game was stopped and started again, and placing a photo needed a mouse. Not measured here.

vindictus.title: Vindictus
vindictus.notes: Vindictus starts through Nexon's Steam connector (nxsteam.exe), a small Electron app that asks for a Nexon account and a server before the game opens. Highball adds Chromium's --in-process-gpu switch when you press Play, which makes the connector's window appear on the default engine. Measured here up to the Nexon sign-in screen only, the game past it is the reporter's. Checked here on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with…

vital-decisions-demo.title: Vital Decisions Demo
vital-decisions-demo.notes: Reported playable on DXVK on macOS 15, a short session.

vital-shell.title: Vital Shell
vital-shell.notes: Reported perfect on an M2 over 89 minutes. The report names WineD3D while the environment was on D3DMetal, so which mode drew the game is not certain.

voices-of-the-void.title: Voices of the Void
voices-of-the-void.notes: Reported playable on DXMT, the default mode, over nearly three hours on an M4. Now and then the game window does not take focus and the game has to be restarted.

vrchat.title: VRChat
vrchat.notes: Anti-cheat: Easy Anti-Cheat. On Windows it loads a kernel driver, which Wine cannot run, and the Linux route (EAC's own Proton runtime) does not exist for macOS, so the launch stops at 'Failed to load the anti-cheat module' on every engine and graphics mode. Linux/Proton status 'Supported' does not apply to macOS.

wanderburg.title: Wanderburg
wanderburg.notes: Reported perfect on the default engine with DXMT on an M1 Pro, over a 26-minute session. Nothing was measured here.

wandering-sword.title: Wandering Sword
wandering-sword.notes: Reported playable on DXMT over an 86-minute session. The report names no problem behind the 4 of 5. No measurement here yet.

war-robots.title: War Robots
war-robots.notes: Reported perfect after a one-minute session on macOS 27.2; the renderer used, frame rate and longer play are not recorded yet. A second perfect report, on DXMT on an M2 with engine r17, a short session of 7 minutes.

warframe.title: Warframe
warframe.notes: Re-verified on engine r2 on 2026-09-10: the launcher updates and starts the game, Login with Steam signs in without typing anything, and the Orbiter runs at 82-94 fps at 1728x1117 fullscreen on DXMT 0.80. Apply the warframe recipe first: it turns DirectWrite off for the game's launcher only (Tools\Launcher.exe), whose embedded browser otherwise paints a black window on this engine, the same DirectWrite problem as…

warhammer-40000-battlesector.title: Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector
warhammer-40000-battlesector.notes: Reported perfect on an M2 Pro with D3DMetal over 65 minutes, on the Wine 11 engine (r28).

warhammer-40000-boltgun.title: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun
warhammer-40000-boltgun.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT on the default engine after a three-minute session, so a start and the first moments of play rather than a full level. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here.

warhammer-dark-omen-classic.title: Warhammer: Dark Omen (Classic)
warhammer-dark-omen-classic.notes: 1998 DirectDraw and Direct3D Retained Mode game, re-released by SNEG with dgVoodoo 2.86 (its ddraw.dll, D3DImm.dll and d3drm.dll sit beside DarkOmen.exe with dgVoodoo.conf). Wine loads its own ddraw in front of those by default, and that path renders nothing: Wine's ddraw logs 'Can't find a flip target' every frame, so the game runs blind (the reporter's finding, reproduced). Letting the bundled dgVoodoo load (DLL…

watch-dogs-2.title: Watch_Dogs® 2
watch-dogs-2.notes: Reported playable on DXMT, the default mode, over a 2-minute session, with a few stutters. Ubisoft Connect's overlay stayed on screen claiming the graphics drivers are outdated, and online play didn't work, which the reporter put down to the anti-cheat. No measurement here yet.

watchmen-the-end-is-nigh.title: Watchmen: The End is Nigh
watchmen-the-end-is-nigh.notes: Doesn't start in one report on an M1. Its MultiLauncher.exe asks for the .NET Framework to be enabled, though .NET 4.8 is installed in the environment. It's a 32-bit game.

waterpark-simulator.title: Waterpark Simulator
waterpark-simulator.notes: Reported perfect on an M4 with DXMT over 42 minutes, with the default settings.

wavetale.title: Wavetale
wavetale.notes: Playable on an M1 on the Wine 11 engine r31, at 25 to 30 fps with frame drops here and there, in a 4 minute session.

wayfinder.title: Wayfinder
wayfinder.notes: An Unreal game that starts in DirectX 12, which DXMT and DXVK do not have. Highball passes -dx11 at Play so it starts in DirectX 11 and plays.

weakless.title: Weakless
weakless.notes: Reported perfect on an M1 with D3DMetal over a short session, mouse and keyboard.

well-dweller.title: Well Dweller
well-dweller.notes: Reported perfect twice on the default engine r7, on an M4 Pro and on an M3 with macOS 15.5, the second one on DXMT after a 35-minute session. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here. On an M1 with macOS 15.7.3 and DXMT on engine r28 it played almost two hours, two boss fights and several areas, with no issues (highball-db#1117).

where-safety-ends-remake.title: WHERE SAFETY ENDS *Remake*
where-safety-ends-remake.notes: A Unity game that opens a fixed 1754x1240 window, set by its own script, so on most Mac screens the window runs past the bottom edge and some screens get cut off. Unity's -screen-width and -screen-height launch options and the saved Screenmanager values do not change it: the game sets the size itself and writes it back. Turn on Retina resolution in the environment's settings: Wine then counts the screen in pixels,…

where-winds-meet.title: Where Winds Meet
where-winds-meet.notes: Free to play. Reported playable on DXMT on the Wine 11 engine with Highball's frame cap at 60 on an M5 Pro, over sessions of 16 minutes and just over three hours without a crash, and one crash about two and a half minutes into a session with the in-game Store window open. Stutter in areas dense with NPCs. The crash is not a one-off, the reporter counted five in two days on highball#240, from 15 seconds to an hour…

while-true-learn.title: while True: learn()
while-true-learn.notes: Reported perfect on an 8 GB M1 MacBook Air with DXMT over 11 minutes on the default engine (r28), at 60 fps at 2K on the game's Ultra Performance setting. The game also has a native Mac version on Steam.

will-you-snail.title: Will You Snail?
will-you-snail.notes: Reported perfect on D3DMetal after a 19-minute session. No measurement here yet.

winter-burrow.title: Winter Burrow
winter-burrow.notes: Reported perfect on an M4 Pro with DXMT over 10 minutes.

wobbly-life.title: Wobbly Life
wobbly-life.notes: Reported perfect on DXMT on an M4 with the default engine r11 after an eight-minute session. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here.

wolfenstein-enemy-territory.title: Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory
wolfenstein-enemy-territory.notes: Free standalone multiplayer game on the id Tech 3 (Quake III) engine, so it renders through OpenGL rather than a Direct3D layer and the graphics mode matters less than for most titles. The one report calls it playable with minor issues after a short session; which issues, the renderer used, and sustained frame rate are not recorded yet.

woman-simulator.title: Woman Simulator
woman-simulator.notes: Reported playable on an M1 with the environment on DXMT, a little laggy. No measurement here yet.

word-link.title: Word Link
word-link.notes: An Electron game. The reporter runs the demo on r11 with DXMT. On an M1 Pro (macOS 27.0) the demo (Steam 5157480) exits three seconds after Steam starts it on the default engine and on r11 alike, with no window and nothing in the log, so the maintainer could not reproduce either half of the report yet. The game rejects Chromium command-line switches (--disable-gpu, --no-sandbox come back as bad options), so launch…

workers-and-resources-soviet-republic.title: Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic
workers-and-resources-soviet-republic.notes: Reported playable on DXMT. The reporter saw some audio and performance issues at very high graphics settings, more than the game's low demands would suggest. No measurement here yet.

world-of-warships.title: World of Warships
world-of-warships.notes: Wargaming ended World of Warships on macOS, and the Windows game refuses to start on a Mac: after the region choice it shows "Sorry, unsupported operating system: macOS support has been discontinued" and quits. It asks Wine which system it runs on and stops when the answer is macOS, so the graphics mode and the engine make no difference. The launcher itself works. The download is 84 GB.

worms-armageddon.title: Worms Armageddon
worms-armageddon.notes: Late-1990s Team17 title, light on the graphics stack. The one report calls it perfect after a short session; renderer used and any edge cases are not recorded yet.

wrath-aeon-of-ruin.title: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin
wrath-aeon-of-ruin.notes: Reported perfect on DXVK with the default engine, close to 120 fps on an M5 Pro, with short hitches the first time new effects load. A native build of the game's engine for Apple silicon and Intel Macs exists at Mac Source Ports (https://www.macsourceports.com/game/wrath). It runs with the game files from a Steam or GOG copy, without achievements (Swiss-Mac-User, highball-db#571).

xcom-enemy-unknown.title: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
xcom-enemy-unknown.notes: Playable on an M4 Max over 108 minutes once set up: a 16:9 resolution such as 2560x1440 rather than ultrawide, and Keep game files inside this environment (the environment's Compatibility settings) so the game's config doesn't live in the Mac's Documents folder.

yakuza-0-directors-cut.title: Yakuza 0 Director's Cut
yakuza-0-directors-cut.notes: Reported perfect on D3DMetal after a session of 1 minute plus about 40 minutes earlier in Whisky. The reporter imported a save from a Whisky bottle and got straight back in-game. No measurement here yet.

yakuza-kiwami.title: Yakuza Kiwami
yakuza-kiwami.notes: The current Steam release of Yakuza Kiwami. Reported perfect on an M4 Pro over almost four hours on an early Wine 11 engine (r10), in an environment in DXVK mode, with D3DMetal by the report.

yandere-simulator.title: Yandere Simulator
yandere-simulator.notes: A Unity game its developer gives away on his own site, not on Steam. Characters' hair stretches into huge black polygons or disappears when the camera moves, in every graphics mode, and turning off Unity's GPU skinning fixes it. Add the line disable-gpu-skinning=1 to boot.config in the game's YandereSimulator_Data folder, add -disable-gpu-skinning to the game's launch arguments in Highball, and clear the game's…

yu-gi-oh-master-duel.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel
yu-gi-oh-master-duel.notes: Reported perfect four times on DXMT on the default engine, most recently on an M5 with r29 and macOS 27.2 (49 minutes, Retina pixels, 60 fps cap). On an M4 Pro with macOS 26.6.2 and engine r5 the Metal HUD hovered around 110 to 120 fps over a 39-minute session, by the reporter's follow-up. On an M4 with macOS 15.7.9, Highball 0.10.3 and engine r19 a 221-minute session was perfect apart from fullscreen being covered…

zero-hour.title: Zero Hour
zero-hour.notes: Anti-cheat: Denuvo Anti-Cheat. Linux/Proton status 'Running' does not apply to macOS.

zero-sievert.title: ZERO Sievert
zero-sievert.notes: Reported perfect on D3DMetal after a short session on an M3 with the steam recipe. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here.

zoria-age-of-shattering.title: Zoria: Age of Shattering
zoria-age-of-shattering.notes: Reported playable on D3DMetal on the default engine. The reporter did not say what the minor issues were. No measurement here yet.
